mainTopic: Do קידושין שאין מסורין לביאה (a betrothal where it is unclear who the wife is) take effect? אביי says yes and רבא says no. The גמרא tests רבא's view against several משניות.
overview: אביי and רבא disagree about קידושין שאין מסורין לביאה, a betrothal that cannot lead to permitted relations because nobody knows which woman is the wife. אביי says it counts, and רבא says it does not. First the גמרא tries to settle this from the משנה about a woman and her relative and the five women with the basket of figs. Each אמורא reads that משנה his own way, so it proves nothing. Next the גמרא challenges רבא from the משנה of a father who betroths 'my daughter' without saying which one. רבא answers that there was only one grown daughter and one minor daughter, and the גמרא explains why the father surely meant the minor. Then come the משנה of two groups of daughters and two cases of sisters whose husbands don't know which one they betrothed. Each time the גמרא answers that the woman was known at first and only later forgotten, pointing to the wording 'he does not know.' When asked what such a משנה would then teach, the גמרא shows its new point: רבי מאיר's view against רבי יוסי, or the later rules about יבום and חליצה. The last of these rules continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Reading the five-women story as 'one of you' to support רבא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests the man in the משנה's story said 'one of you' is betrothed. The sisters are not betrothed, which would support רבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, is the case not that he said to them 'one of you,' and the משנה teaches that the sisters are not betrothed?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא proposes a reading of the משנה's story that would prove רבא's view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the man said 'one of you' and one sister ends up betrothed, he cannot be with either sister, since he does not know which one is his. So the betrothal can never lead to permitted relations. The משנה says the sisters are not betrothed, so such a betrothal would not count, just as רבא holds.

keyTerms.meaning: A betrothal that can never lead to permitted marriage relations

phrases.english: Rather, is it not that he said to them: "One of you"
phrases.notes: This is the man in the משנה's story, who gave a basket of figs to five women, two of whom were sisters.

phrases.english: and it teaches: the sisters are not betrothed?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Comes after the גמרא rejected other readings of the man's words in the story.
steps.raayaObject: רבא's view that קידושין שאין מסורין לביאה are not valid
steps.raayaSupportSource: The end of the משנה: the story of five women and two sisters

steps.title: Each part of the משנה troubles a different side
steps.stepSummary: If the story means 'one of you,' then the end of the משנה is hard for אביי. But the first part of the משנה is hard for רבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: For רבא the first clause is difficult; for אביי the last clause is difficult.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that the משנה cuts both ways: one part challenges רבא and the other part challenges אביי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first part says that betrothing a woman and her daughter 'together' does not work. That suggests betrothing just one of them does work, even though he cannot be with either. That is hard for רבא. The end, read as 'one of you,' says the sisters are not betrothed, which is hard for אביי.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't read the first part of the משנה as supporting רבא. The word כאחת ('together') suggests that betrothing only one of them would work, and that is אביי's view.

phrases.english: For Rava, the first clause is difficult,
phrases.notes: The first clause says: one who betroths a woman and her daughter together, neither is betrothed.

phrases.english: for Abaye, the last clause is difficult.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְרָבָא קַשְׁיָא רֵישָׁא, לְאַבָּיֵי קַשְׁיָא סֵיפָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows that the proof from step 1 is balanced by a problem from the first part of the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: Both אביי (from the end) and רבא (from the beginning)
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The first part implies that betrothing 'one of them' works, which is against רבא. The end, read as 'one of you,' says it doesn't work, which is against אביי.

steps.title: Each side reads the משנה his own way
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא announces that both אביי and רבא can explain the משנה according to their own reasoning.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי explains it according to his reasoning, and רבא explains it according to his reasoning.
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The גמרא announces that each side has an answer, and the next steps lay those answers out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Neither view is knocked out. Each אמורא will reread the part of the משנה that troubles him.

phrases.english: Abaye explains it according to his reasoning,
Rava explains it according to his reasoning.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַבָּיֵי מְתָרֵץ לְטַעְמֵיהּ, רָבָא מְתָרֵץ לְטַעְמֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the double difficulty in a general way, before giving the details.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Each side rereads the משנה to fit his view

steps.title: אביי keeps the first clause as it reads
steps.stepSummary: אביי reads the first clause plainly: betrothing both together fails, but betrothing 'one of them' works.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי explains: one who betroths a woman and her daughter, or a woman and her sister, together — they are not betrothed. But one of a woman and her daughter, or of a woman and her sister — she is betrothed.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי reads the first part of the משנה exactly as it sounds, which fits his view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Betrothing both at once fails, because he cannot marry both relatives. But if he says 'one of you,' a betrothal takes effect, even though he cannot be with either one. That fits אביי's view that such a betrothal counts.

phrases.english: Abaye explains it according to his reasoning:
One who betroths a woman and her daughter,
or a woman and her sister, together —
they are not betrothed.
But one of a woman and her daughter,
or of a woman and her sister — she is betrothed.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַבָּיֵי מְתָרֵץ לְטַעְמֵיהּ: הַמְקַדֵּשׁ אִשָּׁה וּבִתָּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts אביי's detailed answer.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reading the first clause plainly, as supporting him
steps.terutzMaskana: Betrothing 'one of' two forbidden relatives works, even though he cannot be with either.

steps.title: אביי rereads the story as 'the one fit for relations'
steps.stepSummary: For אביי, the story is about a man who said 'the one fit for relations with me.' That is why neither sister is betrothed.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if he said, 'The one fit for relations shall be betrothed to me,' she is not betrothed. And there was also a story with five women, two of them sisters. A man gathered a basket of figs and said, 'The one among you fit for me shall be betrothed to me,' and the חכמים said: the sisters are not betrothed.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי explains that the man in the story made a condition: 'the one fit for me.' That is why the sisters were not betrothed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Neither sister can be singled out as 'fit,' because each is forbidden if the other is his wife. So his condition is never met, and neither sister is betrothed. The story therefore says nothing about a plain 'one of you,' and אביי's view stands.

keyTerms.meaning: The one fit (halachically permitted) for relations

phrases.english: And if he said: "The one fit for relations shall be betrothed to me" —
she is not betrothed.
And there was also an incident with five women,
and among them were two sisters,
and one man gathered a basket of figs
and said: "The one among you fit for me shall be betrothed to me,"
and the Sages said: the sisters are not betrothed.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִם אָמַר: הָרְאוּיָה לְבִיאָה תִּתְקַדֵּשׁ לִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes אביי's answer by rereading the last clause.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the case in the last clause
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The man said 'one of you,' which would prove רבא right.
steps.terutzMaskana: The man said 'the one fit for me,' and no sister meets that condition.

steps.title: רבא rereads the first clause and the story
steps.stepSummary: For רבא, betrothing 'one of' two relatives is just like betrothing both together, so neither is betrothed. In the story, the man said 'all of you and one of the two sisters.'
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבא explains according to his reasoning: one who betroths one of a woman and her daughter, or one of a woman and her sister, it is as if he betrothed a woman and her daughter, or a woman and her sister, together, and they are not betrothed. And there was also a story with five women, two of them sisters. A man gathered a basket of figs and said, 'All of you, and one of the two sisters, are betrothed to me with this basket,' and the חכמים said: the sisters are not betrothed.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא explains both parts of the משנה so that they fit his view that such a betrothal does not count.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא reads כאחת as including a case of 'one of them,' since it is treated like betrothing both together. He reads the story as 'all of you and one of the sisters.' Then the משנה teaches that the sisters are not betrothed, while the other three women are. Since both readings work, the משנה cannot settle the argument.
steps.whatToRemember: אביי holds that קידושין שאין מסורין לביאה count, and רבא holds they don't. The משנה about the woman and her relative, and the five women, can be read to fit either view, so it is no proof.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a common pattern in the גמרא: when a source can be read in two ways, it cannot decide a dispute.

phrases.english: And Rava explains it according to his reasoning:
One who betroths one of a woman and her daughter
or one of a woman and her sister —
it becomes like one who betrothed a woman and her daughter,
or a woman and her sister, together,
and they are not betrothed.
And there was also an incident with five women,
and among them were two sisters,
and one man gathered a basket of figs

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמַר: הֲרֵי כּוּלְּכֶם וְאַחַת מִשְׁתֵּי אֲחָיוֹת
phrases.english: and said: All of you, and one of the two sisters,
phrases.notes: 'All of you' means the three women who are not sisters.

phrases.english: are betrothed to me with this basket,
and the Sages said: the sisters are not betrothed.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרָבָא מְתָרֵץ לְטַעְמֵיהּ: הַמְקַדֵּשׁ אַחַת מֵאִשָּׁה וּבִתָּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives רבא's reading, alongside אביי's reading in steps 4–5.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the first clause and redefining the case in the story
steps.terutzHavaAmina: כאחת implies that betrothing 'one of them' works, which would be against רבא.
steps.terutzMaskana: Betrothing 'one of them' is treated like betrothing both together, so it fails. The story involved 'all of you and one of the sisters.'

steps.title: A משנה that seems to refute רבא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a משנה about a father who betroths 'my daughter' without saying which one. It seems to show that unclear קידושין do take effect, against רבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: if a man betroths 'his daughter' without saying which one, the grown daughters are not included. That means the minor daughters are included. But why? Those are קידושין that cannot lead to relations, since we don't know which girl it is. So this refutes רבא!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a משנה and reads an implication from it. That implication seems to break רבא's view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Grown daughters are left out because a father cannot betroth them. That leaves the minor daughters inside the doubt, which means some kind of קידושין took effect on them. But with several minors, nobody knows who the wife is, so these are 'קידושין שאין מסורין לביאה.' רבא said such קידושין do not work.

keyTerms.meaning: Come and hear: the גמרא is bringing a source
Minor daughters, whom the father can betroth
Betrothal that cannot lead to permitted relations, since it is unclear who the wife is

steps.confusionAlert: The proof comes from what the משנה implies ('הא'), not from its actual words. The משנה only says the grown daughters are left out.

phrases.english: Come and hear:
One who betroths his daughter without specifying which one,
phrases.notes: This is a משנה found later in this מסכת.

phrases.english: the grown daughters are not included.
This implies that the minor daughters are included.
But why?
It is a betrothal that is not given over to relations,
phrases.notes: He never said which minor daughter he meant, so he can't be with any one of them for sure.

phrases.english: and this is a refutation of Rava!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After both אביי and רבא explained the first משנה, the גמרא brings a new source against רבא.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's rule that קידושין שאין מסורין לביאה do not take effect
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה implies the minor daughters are betrothed even though it is unclear which one is the wife.

steps.title: רבא: only one grown and one minor daughter
steps.stepSummary: רבא says the משנה is talking about a father with just one grown daughter and one minor daughter.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא could answer you: what case is this? When there is only one grown daughter and one minor daughter.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא narrows the case in the משנה so that his rule is not broken.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the grown daughter is ruled out, only one minor daughter is left. So it is clear exactly who is betrothed. These קידושין can lead to relations, and רבא's rule is not touched.

keyTerms.meaning: He could say to you: the גמרא answering for someone
With what case are we dealing here?

phrases.english: Rava could say to you:
With what are we dealing here?
When there is only one grown daughter and one minor daughter.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לָךְ רָבָא הָכָא בְּמַאי עָסְקִינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge against רבא.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה speaks of several minor daughters, so the קידושין are unclear.
steps.terutzMaskana: There is only one minor daughter, so it is clear who is betrothed.

steps.title: But the משנה says 'grown daughters' in the plural
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects: the משנה uses the plural 'grown daughters,' so it seems there are several.
steps.simpleTranslation: But the משנה says 'grown daughters'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רבא's answer by pointing at a word in the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the father has just one grown daughter, the משנה should have said 'the grown daughter.' The plural suggests a family with several daughters. That would bring back the problem of several minors too.

phrases.english: But it teaches 'grown daughters' (plural)!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבא's limited case from the wording of the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's claim that there is only one grown daughter
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The plural wording doesn't fit a family with only one grown daughter.

steps.title: 'Grown daughters' means grown daughters in general
steps.stepSummary: The plural is speaking about all people in general, not about one father's family.
steps.simpleTranslation: What does 'grown daughters' mean? Grown daughters in general.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the plural word so that רבא's case still works.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה is stating a general rule for every father: grown daughters are never included. Each father in the case still has only one grown daughter. So the plural doesn't prove anything.

keyTerms.meaning: Of the world, meaning in general
Grown daughters of all people in general

phrases.english: What does 'grown daughters' mean?
Grown daughters in general.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the plural-wording challenge.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The plural means one family has several grown daughters.
steps.terutzMaskana: The plural is a general rule for all fathers.

steps.title: If so, what is the משנה teaching?
steps.stepSummary: If there is just one grown daughter and one minor daughter, the answer seems obvious. So why does the משנה need to say it?
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, why does it need to be said?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what new idea the משנה would be teaching in רבא's case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A father obviously cannot betroth his grown daughter, so of course his words go to the minor daughter. A משנה is expected to teach something new. This sets up the final answer.

keyTerms.meaning: What is there to say? (meaning: it's obvious)

phrases.english: If so, what is the point of saying it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Accepts the reading of the plural but says רבא's case makes the משנה pointless.
steps.kashyaTarget: The case of one grown daughter and one minor daughter
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In that case the ruling is obvious, so the משנה would teach nothing new.

steps.title: The grown daughter made her father her agent
steps.stepSummary: The grown daughter had appointed her father to accept קידושין for her. Still, we assume he meant the minor daughter, because he benefits from her קידושין.
steps.simpleTranslation: What case is this? The grown daughter made him her agent. You might think that when he accepts קידושין, he accepts them for her. So the משנה teaches us that a person does not give up something he gets benefit from.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the new idea the משנה teaches, which saves רבא. The next step challenges the reason given here.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the father was her agent, he really could have betrothed the grown daughter. That creates a real doubt. The משנה rules he meant the minor daughter, whose קידושין money goes to him. He would not choose the grown daughter, who keeps her own money.

keyTerms.meaning: You might have said (the mistaken thought)

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה works even for רבא. It speaks of one grown and one minor daughter, and teaches that a father means the daughter he benefits from: the minor.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows the principle 'לא שביק איניש מידי דאית ליה הנאה מיניה.' We read a person's unclear words by what benefits him.

phrases.english: With what are we dealing here?
Where she made him her agent.
phrases.notes: 'She' is the grown daughter. She asked her father to accept קידושין for her.

phrases.english: You might have said
that when he accepts betrothal
he accepts it with her in mind,
so it teaches us
that a person does not leave aside
something he gets benefit from.
phrases.notes: The father keeps a minor daughter's קידושין money, but a grown daughter keeps her own.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers 'מאי למימרא' by adding a detail that gives the משנה a new idea.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Adding a detail to the case to show its new idea
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since he was her agent, he meant to betroth the grown daughter.
steps.terutzMaskana: He meant the minor daughter, whose קידושין money he keeps. So the קידושין are clear, and רבא stands.

steps.title: Maybe the father benefits from the grown daughter too
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges step 12: perhaps the grown daughter told her father her קידושין money is his, so he gains from her too.
steps.simpleTranslation: Aren't we dealing with a case where the grown daughter told him: 'My קידושין money is yours'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is poking a hole in the last answer. It says the father might gain from the grown daughter's קידושין as well, so 'he benefits' cannot be the reason he meant the minor.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 12 said we assume the father meant the minor daughter because her קידושין money goes to him. But a grown daughter can choose to give her קידושין money to her father. If she did, he gains from both daughters, and the reason from step 12 no longer picks out the minor.

keyTerms.meaning: Aren't we dealing with... (a question that offers another possible case)

phrases.english: Aren't we dealing
with a case where she said to him: 'My betrothal money is yours'?
phrases.notes: 'She' is the grown daughter. Normally her קידושין money would belong to her, but here she hands it over to her father.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the reason given in step 12.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim in step 12 that the father meant the minor because only her קידושין benefits him.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the grown daughter gave him her קידושין money, he benefits from both daughters equally, so benefit cannot decide which one he meant.

steps.title: A person does not drop his own מצוה for someone else's
steps.stepSummary: Even so, the father would still mean the minor, because marrying her off is his מצוה and marrying off the grown daughter is not.
steps.simpleTranslation: Even so, a person does not leave a מצוה that is his responsibility and do a מצוה that is not his responsibility.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. Even if he gains from both daughters, he would still choose the one whose קידושין is his own job.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The reason now moves from money to responsibility. Arranging the קידושין of a minor daughter is the father's job, while a grown daughter arranges her own. So we assume he did the מצוה that was on him and meant the minor.

keyTerms.meaning: lies upon him, is his responsibility

steps.whatToRemember: The father is assumed to have meant the minor daughter. This is not only because he gains from her, but because her קידושין is a מצוה that is his responsibility.

phrases.english: Even so,

phrases.aramaic: לָא שָׁבֵיק אִינִישׁ מִצְוָה דְּרַמְיָא עֲלֵיהּ
phrases.english: a person does not leave a מצוה that is his responsibility
phrases.notes: That is the קידושין of his minor daughter, which is his job.

phrases.english: and do a מצוה that is not his responsibility.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲפִילּוּ הָכִי, לָא שָׁבֵיק אִינִישׁ מִצְוָה דְּרַמְיָא עֲלֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 13.
steps.terutzResolutionType: New reason that keeps the earlier conclusion
steps.terutzHavaAmina: If he benefits from both daughters, we cannot tell which one he meant.
steps.terutzMaskana: He meant the minor, because her קידושין is his own מצוה and the grown daughter's is not.

steps.title: The case of two groups of daughters
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a משנה: a father with two groups of daughters betrothed 'my older daughter' and does not know which one. According to רבי מאיר, all are forbidden except the very youngest.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: A man has two groups of daughters from two wives. He said: 'I betrothed my older daughter, and I do not know if it was the oldest of the older group, or the oldest of the younger group, or the youngest of the older group, who is older than the oldest of the younger group.' All of them are forbidden, except the youngest of the younger group. These are the words of רבי מאיר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new source that seems to work against רבא. Here the קידושין is unclear, yet it still takes effect on every daughter who might be the one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: No single daughter can just go live with the husband, because any of them might be the sister of his real wife. So this קידושין cannot lead right away to married life. Yet all the daughters are treated as possibly betrothed and need a גט. That suggests such קידושין do take effect.

keyTerms.meaning: the oldest of the older group
the youngest of the younger group
forbidden (to marry anyone else without a גט)

steps.confusionAlert: Here 'older' and 'younger' are about age compared to the other daughters. They are not the legal terms for a grown daughter and a minor that we saw earlier.

phrases.english: Come and hear:

phrases.aramaic: מִי שֶׁיֵּשׁ לוֹ שְׁתֵּי כִּתֵּי בָנוֹת
phrases.english: One who has two groups of daughters
from two wives,
and he said: 'I betrothed my older daughter,
and I do not know if it is the oldest of the older group
or the oldest of the younger group,
or the youngest of the older group
who is older than the oldest of the younger group'
all of them are forbidden,
except for the youngest of the younger group,
these are the words of Rabbi Meir.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע: מִי שֶׁיֵּשׁ לוֹ שְׁתֵּי כִּתֵּי בָנוֹת מִשְׁתֵּי נָשִׁים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the case of one grown daughter and one minor, and brings a new source on the main question.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's view that קידושין שאין מסורין לביאה do not take effect.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In this משנה no daughter can go live with the husband, yet the קידושין takes effect, since all of them need a גט.

steps.title: He knew which daughter at first, then forgot
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof: the father clearly named one daughter at the time of the קידושין and only later forgot which one.
steps.simpleTranslation: What are we dealing with here? When they were identified, and in the end they got mixed up.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes away the proof. It explains the משנה as a case where the קידושין was clear when it was done, and the doubt came only afterward.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the father named one specific daughter at the time, the קידושין could lead to married life, so it was a normal, valid קידושין. The daughters are forbidden only because we no longer know which one it was. So this משנה tells us nothing about קידושין that were unclear from the start.

keyTerms.meaning: What are we dealing with here? (narrowing a source to a specific case)

phrases.english: With what are we dealing here?
When they were identified and in the end got mixed up.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָכָא בְּמַאי עָסְקִינַן, כְּשֶׁהוּכְּרוּ וּלְבַסּוֹף נִתְעָרְבוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof brought in step 15.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Full rejection of the proof from this משנה
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumed the קידושין was unclear from the start. In fact it was clear at first and only became unclear later.
steps.terutzMaskana: The father named a specific daughter and only later forgot which one, so the קידושין could lead to married life when it was made, and רבא's view stands.

steps.title: The words 'I do not know' support this reading
steps.stepSummary: The משנה's wording, 'I do not know' rather than 'it is not known,' shows he once knew and later forgot.
steps.simpleTranslation: The wording is also exact, because it teaches 'I do not know' and does not teach 'it is not known.' Learn from it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up its new reading from the exact words of the משנה. 'I do not know' sounds like a person who once knew and forgot.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'It is not known' would suggest that nobody ever knew which daughter was meant. 'I do not know' points to the father's own memory, so the doubt came later. This supports the reading in step 16.

keyTerms.meaning: The wording is also exact (supports this reading)

phrases.english: The wording is also exact,
since it teaches: 'I do not know,'
and it does not teach: 'It is not known.'
Learn from it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the rejection in step 16.
steps.raayaObject: That the משנה is about daughters who were identified and then got mixed up.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה's wording 'I do not know' rather than 'it is not known.'

steps.title: Then what is the משנה teaching?
steps.stepSummary: If he simply forgot which daughter, of course all of them are in doubt, so what is new?
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, what is it coming to tell us?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges its own reading. If the father just forgot, the result seems obvious, so why would the משנה need to say it?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the case is just 'he knew and forgot,' there seems to be nothing new to learn. The גמרא is setting up the next step, which will show what the משנה is really teaching.

keyTerms.meaning: What is there to say? Why teach it?

phrases.english: If so, what is the point of saying it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reading set up in steps 16 and 17.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading that the daughters were identified and later mixed up.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If so, the ruling is obvious, and a משנה should not need to teach something obvious.

steps.title: רבי מאיר disagrees with רבי יוסי about putting oneself in doubt
steps.stepSummary: The משנה teaches, against רבי יוסי, that a person does put himself into a doubtful situation. So 'older daughter' could mean more than just the very oldest.
steps.simpleTranslation: It comes to exclude the view of רבי יוסי, who says a person does not put himself into a doubt. It teaches us that a person does put himself into a doubt.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the משנה's point is a disagreement. רבי יוסי says 'my older daughter' must mean the very oldest, while רבי מאיר says it could mean several daughters.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רבי יוסי, a person speaks clearly, so 'older daughter' means only the very oldest and nobody else is in doubt. רבי מאיר holds that a person may use a word that could fit several daughters. That is why all of them except the very youngest are forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: a person puts himself into a doubt

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה of the two groups of daughters is a case where he knew which daughter and later forgot. Its new point is רבי מאיר's view, against רבי יוסי, that a person does put himself into a doubtful situation.

phrases.english: To exclude the view of Rabbi Yosei,

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר: לָא מַחֵית אִינִישׁ נַפְשֵׁיהּ לִסְפֵיקָא.
phrases.english: who says: A person does not put himself into a doubt.
phrases.notes: So for רבי יוסי, 'my older daughter' means only the very oldest one.

phrases.english: It teaches us
that a person does put himself into a doubt.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 18.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows the new teaching is a disagreement with another תנא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ruling seems obvious, so the משנה teaches nothing new.
steps.terutzMaskana: It teaches, against רבי יוסי, that a person does put himself into a doubt, so many daughters could be the one meant.

steps.title: A man betrothed one of two sisters and does not know which
steps.stepSummary: A new challenge from a משנה: a man betrothed one of two sisters, does not know which, and must give a גט to each. So the betrothal seems to work even though he can never live with either sister.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: if a man betrothed one of two sisters and does not know which one, he gives a גט to this one and a גט to that one.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another משנה to challenge the view that a betrothal which cannot lead to living together does not take effect.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since he does not know which sister is his, he can never live with either one, because she might be the sister of his wife. Even so, the משנה requires a גט for each. That suggests a betrothal that cannot lead to marriage still takes effect.

keyTerms.meaning: Come and hear: the גמרא is bringing a source as a proof or a challenge
A wife's sister, who is forbidden to him
A betrothal that can never lead to the couple living together

phrases.english: Come and hear:
One who betrothed one of two sisters
and he does not know which one he betrothed
gives a get to this one and a get to that one.
phrases.notes: Here is the problem: he can't live with either sister, yet the משנה still treats the betrothal as real.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע: מִי שֶׁקִּידֵּשׁ אַחַת מִשְׁתֵּי אֲחָיוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the daughters case was resolved, the גמרא brings a new משנה with the same kind of challenge.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's view that קידושין שאין מסורין לביאה do not take effect
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The man can never live with either sister, but the משנה still requires two גיטין. So the betrothal must have taken effect.

steps.title: He knew which sister at first and forgot later
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the case is where he betrothed a specific, known sister, and only afterward the two got mixed up in his mind.
steps.simpleTranslation: What case are we dealing with here? Where the sisters were known apart at first, and only later got mixed up.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by narrowing the case: at the moment of betrothal it was clear which sister he was marrying.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When he betrothed her, she was a known woman he was fully allowed to live with. So this betrothal could lead to marriage. The doubt came only afterward, so this case says nothing about a betrothal that could never lead to marriage.

keyTerms.meaning: What case are we dealing with here? The גמרא is about to narrow the case
They were identified or known apart

phrases.english: Here, what are we dealing with?
When they were identified, and in the end they got mixed up.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָכָא בְּמַאי עָסְקִינַן, כְּשֶׁהוּכְּרוּ וּלְבַסּוֹף נִתְעָרְבוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 20 the same way step 16 answered the daughters case.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The man never knew which sister he betrothed, so the betrothal could never lead to marriage.
steps.terutzMaskana: He betrothed a known sister and forgot later, so at the time the betrothal could lead to marriage.

steps.title: The wording 'he does not know' supports the answer
steps.stepSummary: The משנה says 'he does not know,' not 'it is not known.' That fits a man who once knew and later forgot.
steps.simpleTranslation: The wording is exact too: it says 'he does not know,' and not 'it is not known.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up its answer from the exact words of the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'He does not know' describes the man's own forgetting, which means there was a clear fact he once knew. 'It is not known' would describe a case that was never clear to begin with.

keyTerms.meaning: The wording is also exact: support from the precise language
He does not know: he personally forgot
It is not known: it was never clear at all

phrases.english: It is also precise,
for it teaches: "he does not know,"
and it does not teach: "it is not known."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the answer in step 21, just as step 17 supported step 16.
steps.raayaObject: The answer that he knew at first and forgot later

steps.title: Then what is new in this משנה?
steps.stepSummary: If he just forgot which sister, it is obvious that both are in doubt and both need a גט. So what does the משנה teach?
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, why does it need to be said?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on its own answer: if this is just a case of forgetting, the ruling seems too obvious to need saying.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A valid betrothal followed by a mix-up obviously means both women are in doubt. The question is why the משנה would bother to state something so simple. This sets up the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: If so: if your answer is right
Why does it need to be said? It seems obvious

phrases.english: If so, what is there to say?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of step 21 by asking what the משנה would then be teaching, like step 18.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If he simply forgot, requiring a גט for both is obvious, and a משנה should not state the obvious.

steps.title: The point is the later clause about יבום and חליצה
steps.stepSummary: The first part is only background. The real lesson is in the later clause: what happens when the man dies and his brothers face these two sisters.
steps.simpleTranslation: The later part was needed: if he died and had one brother, that brother does חליצה with both sisters. If he had two brothers, one does חליצה and the other does יבום. If they went ahead and married both, we do not take the wives away from them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the first clause is just a setup, and the new teaching is in the later rules about יבום and חליצה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With one brother, he cannot do יבום with either sister, because she might be the sister of the woman bound to him. So he does חליצה with both. With two brothers, one does חליצה with one sister, and then the other may do יבום with the other. If both brothers already married the sisters, the court lets the marriages stand.

keyTerms.meaning: The later part of the משנה
It was needed: this is where the new teaching is
Does חליצה, the ceremony that frees the widow from יבום
Does יבום, marrying his late brother's widow
We do not take them away from them: the marriage is left standing

phrases.english: The latter clause was needed for it:
If he died and he had one brother,
he does חליצה with both of them.
phrases.notes: He can't do יבום with either one, since she might be the sister of the woman bound to him.

phrases.english: If he had two (brothers),
one does חליצה and one does יבום.
If they went ahead and married them,
we do not take them out of their hands.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 23 by moving the משנה's new teaching to its later clause.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Moving the new teaching to another clause (סיפא איצטריכא ליה)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה is pointless if the man simply forgot.
steps.terutzMaskana: The first clause is background; the משנה was written for the יבום and חליצה rules that follow.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a common pattern in the גמרא: an obvious first clause can be there only to set up a later clause that really teaches something new.

steps.title: Only חליצה first, then יבום
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא spells out the new teaching: the order matters. חליצה must come first. If יבום comes first, the brother may be marrying the sister of the woman bound to him.
steps.simpleTranslation: This works only if one brother does חליצה first and then the other does יבום. If one does יבום first and then the other does חליצה, it does not work, because he is meeting the sister of the woman bound to him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains exactly what is new in the later clause: the order of חליצה and יבום matters.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until one sister is freed by חליצה, each sister is like a 'wife's sister' to both brothers, because of the bond of יבום. Once חליצה frees one sister, the other brother may do יבום with the remaining one. If he does יבום first, he may be taking the sister of the woman still bound to him.

keyTerms.meaning: The sister of the woman bound to him for יבום

phrases.english: Specifically doing חליצה first and afterward doing יבום,
but doing יבום first and afterward חליצה, no,
because he is coming upon the sister of the woman bound to him.
phrases.notes: 'Bound to him' means tied to him by the bond of יבום, which makes her sister off-limits for now.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the answer of step 24 by stating the exact new rule found in the later clause.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: One might think the order of חליצה and יבום does not matter.
steps.terutzMaskana: חליצה must come first. יבום first is not allowed, because of זיקה to the sister.
steps.confusionAlert: The brother who does יבום first is not marrying a sister he knows is forbidden. The problem is that, without knowing which sister is which, either one might be the sister of the woman still bound to him.

steps.title: Two men betrothed two sisters and neither knows which
steps.stepSummary: A further challenge from the same משנה: two men each betrothed one of two sisters, and neither knows which one. Each must give two גיטין. So again the betrothal seems to take effect even though it can never lead to marriage.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: two men betrothed two sisters. This one does not know which he betrothed, and that one does not know which he betrothed. This one gives two גיטין, and that one gives two גיטין!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the next case in the same משנה to challenge the same view again.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Neither man can live with either sister, since any of the four pairings might be wrong. Still, each must divorce both women. That looks like proof that a betrothal which cannot lead to marriage takes effect.

phrases.aramaic: תָּא שְׁמַע: שְׁנַיִם שֶׁקִּדְּשׁוּ שְׁתֵּי אֲחָיוֹת,
phrases.english: Come and hear: Two men who betrothed two sisters,
this one does not know which he betrothed
and that one does not know which he betrothed,
this one gives two gittin,
and that one gives two gittin!

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע: שְׁנַיִם שֶׁקִּדְּשׁוּ שְׁתֵּי אֲחָיוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a second, similar case from the same משנה after step 20's challenge was answered.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's view that קידושין שאין מסורין לביאה do not take effect
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Neither man can live with either sister, yet each must give two גיטין, so the betrothals must have taken effect.

steps.title: Same answer: they were known first and mixed up later
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא gives the same answer: each man betrothed a known sister, and the mix-up came only later.
steps.simpleTranslation: Here too, it is where they were identified at first and later got mixed up.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers this challenge exactly the way it answered step 20.
steps.deeperAnalysis: At the time of betrothal, each man married a known woman he was allowed to live with. So each betrothal could lead to marriage, and the later confusion does not change that.

keyTerms.meaning: Here too: the same answer applies

phrases.english: Here too, where they were identified, and in the end they got mixed up.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 26 by using the same narrowed case as step 21.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Neither man ever knew which sister he betrothed.
steps.terutzMaskana: Each betrothed a known sister and later forgot which one.

steps.title: The wording proves it, and the גמרא accepts it
steps.stepSummary: Again the wording 'he does not know' shows that each man once knew. The גמרא closes with שמע מינה: we have learned it from here.
steps.simpleTranslation: The wording is exact too: it says 'he does not know,' and not 'it is not known.' Learn from it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא supports its answer from the wording and confirms it with שמע מינה. The next step then asks what this part of the משנה is teaching.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The same wording point as in step 22 shows the case is about forgetting, not a case that was never clear. With שמע מינה, the גמרא accepts the reading. The challenges from the sisters case fail to disprove the view being defended.

keyTerms.meaning: Learn from it: the point is accepted as proven
It is not known (another form of the same phrase)

phrases.english: It is also precise, for it teaches: "he does not know,"
and it does not teach: "it is not known,"
learn from it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the answer of step 27 with שמע מינה, just as step 22 supported step 21.
steps.raayaObject: The answer that the sisters were known first and mixed up later
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה's wording 'אינו יודע' rather than 'אין ידוע'
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The sisters cases deal with a betrothal that was clear at first and confused later, so they do not prove that a betrothal which cannot lead to marriage takes effect.
steps.whatToRemember: Every משנה here that seemed to show such a betrothal works is explained the same way: he knew which woman at first and only forgot later. The wording 'אינו יודע' (he does not know) is the clue each time.

steps.title: If each man knew at first, what is new here?
steps.stepSummary: If each man once knew which sister he betrothed, then of course each must give two גיטין. So what is the משנה teaching?
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, what is the point of saying it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on its own answer. If each man betrothed a known sister and only later forgot, the rule seems too obvious to need a משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 27 the גמרא said each man betrothed a specific sister and the mix-up came later. That keeps the betrothal valid. But it creates a new problem: a valid betrothal followed by doubt obviously calls for a גט to each sister, so this part of the משנה seems to add nothing.

keyTerms.meaning: If so; if that is how you explain it
What is the point of saying it? Isn't it obvious?

phrases.english: If so, what is the point of saying it?
phrases.notes: "If so" points back to the answer that each man first knew which sister he betrothed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer from steps 27-28. Once that answer is accepted, the משנה's ruling looks obvious.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's ruling that each man gives two גיטין, as now explained.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A valid betrothal of a known sister, followed by forgetting which one, obviously needs a גט to each sister. A משנה should not teach the obvious.

steps.title: The real lesson is in the later clause about the brothers
steps.stepSummary: The משנה needed the later clause: if the men die and each has a brother, each brother does חליצה with both sisters. The גמרא then starts quoting the next case, where one man has one brother and the other has two.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was needed for the later clause: if he died, and this one had a brother and that one had a brother, this brother does חליצה with both of them and that brother does חליצה with both of them. If this one had one brother and that one had two...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the first part is only background, and the new teaching is what the brothers do after the men die. It then begins quoting the next case, which continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each brother does not know which sister was his own brother's wife, so he must do חליצה with both sisters. He cannot do יבום, because the woman he marries might be the sister of the woman who is really tied to him. The case of one brother on one side and two on the other is only set up here; its ruling comes on the next amud.

keyTerms.meaning: The later clause of the משנה
It was needed; that is why he taught it
Does חֲלִיצָה, the ceremony that frees a widow from marrying her late husband's brother
When a brother marries his childless brother's widow

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two pairs. The two sisters are the women, the two men who died are their possible husbands, and "this one" and "that one" are those dead men. Each dead man has his own brother.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the same move as steps 24-25. When a clause in the משנה looks obvious, the גמרא shows it is background for a later clause with a real new teaching.

phrases.english: The later clause is what he needed:
If he died, and this one had a brother and that one had a brother,
phrases.notes: "This one" and "that one" are the two men who betrothed the sisters, and both of them died.

phrases.english: this brother does חליצה with both of them,
and that brother does חליצה with both of them.
If this one had one brother and that one had two,
phrases.notes: The sentence stops here. The ruling for this case comes on the next amud.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 29 by moving the משנה's new lesson to its later clause.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Moving the new teaching to the later clause of the משנה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The case seemed to teach nothing, because two גיטין is obvious.
steps.terutzMaskana: The case is background for the new teaching: after the men die, each brother must do חליצה with both sisters and may not do יבום.
